title: Core Switch VLAN Mismatch & Packet Drop Troubleshooting
body:
### Problem Overview
Inter-VLAN traffic between engineering subnets and internal services experiences intermittent 100% packet loss or severe throughput throttling. Typically caused by 802.1Q trunk native VLAN mismatches or spanning-tree loop-guard blocks.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. SSH into the switch and verify port trunk negotiation: `show interfaces trunk`
2. Inspect Native VLAN configuration: `show vlan brief`
3. Check for spanning tree topology change notifications: `show spanning-tree detail | include is executing`
4. Verify CRC frame error counts on physical uplink: `show interfaces GigabitEthernet1/0/1 counters errors`

### Resolution SOP
1. Ensure both ends of the 802.1Q trunk share the identical native VLAN (e.g. VLAN 999 default).
2. Re-enable STP portfast on client edge access ports: `spanning-tree portfast edge`
3. Clear dynamic MAC address learning table: `clear mac address-table dynamic interface Gi1/0/1`
4. Run continuous ping from source subnet to verify 0% packet drop: `ping -c 50 10.10.20.1`

title: Subnet DHCP Scope Exhaustion and IP Allocation Failures
body:
### Problem Overview
Workstations connecting to the corporate LAN or office Wi-Fi receive an APIPA address (169.254.x.x) with error 'DHCP lookup failed: No offer received'. The DHCP server has exhausted all available leases.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. In Windows PowerShell (DHCP Server): `Get-DhcpServerv4ScopeStatistics -ScopeId 10.150.0.0`
2. Identify expired or stale leases not reclaimed: `Get-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId 10.150.0.0 -AllLeases | Measure-Object`
3. Verify IP helper-address on edge gateway: `show running-config interface Vlan150 | include ip helper`

### Resolution SOP
1. Shorten DHCP lease duration from 8 days to 4 hours in dynamic hot-desking offices.
2. Force-reclaim dead leases: `Remove-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId 10.150.0.0 -BadLeases`
3. Expand scope mask from /24 to /23 if client density permanently increased.
4. On client workstation, release and renew: `ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew`

title: Internal DNS Resolution Failures and Recursive Forwarder Timeouts
body:
### Problem Overview
Internal microservices and intranet hostnames fail to resolve (NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL), while external sites resolve normally. Occurs when internal BIND/Windows DNS conditional forwarders become unresponsive.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Test internal query: `nslookup internal-auth.corp.local 10.0.0.53`
2. Check DNS response flags and query latency: `dig @10.0.0.53 internal-auth.corp.local +trace`
3. Inspect DNS service logs on primary domain controller: Event ID 4015 / 4004 (DNS Server).

### Resolution SOP
1. Restart DNS server service: `Restart-Service DNS` (or `systemctl restart named`).
2. Flush internal resolver cache: `Clear-DnsServerCache` on server and `ipconfig /flushdns` on clients.
3. Verify upstream DNS forwarder root hints IP addresses are updated and reachable over UDP/TCP port 53.

title: Enterprise Wi-Fi 802.1X RADIUS Authentication Failures
body:
### Problem Overview
Laptops and corporate mobile devices fail to associate with the 'Corporate-Secure' WPA3-Enterprise SSID. Clients report 'Can't connect to this network' after entering valid enterprise credentials.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check NPS/FreeRADIUS accounting log for EAP-TLS / PEAP-MSCHAPv2 failure code 16 (Auth Failure).
2. Verify RADIUS server SSL certificate expiration date.
3. Inspect intermediate CA trust chain on client device using `certmgr.msc`.

### Resolution SOP
1. If the RADIUS certificate expired, renew it on the Enterprise Root CA and rebind in NPS.
2. Push the updated Root and Intermediate CA certs to devices via Microsoft Intune / Jamf profile.
3. On Windows clients, forget the Wi-Fi profile: `netsh wlan delete profile name="Corporate-Secure"` and reconnect.

title: Asymmetric Routing and MTU Blackhole Packet Fragmentation
body:
### Problem Overview
Large file downloads or SSH connections freeze immediately after negotiation (during TLS handshake or key exchange). Ping works, but TCP sessions stall due to Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) packet drops by stateful firewalls.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Test max MTU without fragmentation: `ping -f -l 1472 <target-ip>` (Windows) or `ping -M do -s 1472 <target-ip>` (Linux).
2. Check router WAN interface MTU and MSS clamping configuration: `show interface GigabitEthernet0/0 | include MTU`
3. Inspect firewall ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) filter rules.

### Resolution SOP
1. Enable TCP MSS clamping on VPN and GRE tunnels: `ip tcp adjust-mss 1360` on WAN interfaces.
2. Ensure edge firewalls do not block ICMP Type 3 (Destination Unreachable / Fragmentation Needed).
3. Temporarily set client MTU to 1420 for verification: `netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "Ethernet" mtu=1420 store=persistent`

title: Exchange Online / M365 Inbound Mail Delivery Latency & Queue Backlog
body:
### Problem Overview
External emails to corporate inboxes are delayed by 45 to 120 minutes. Sender domains receive delayed delivery notices. Caused by throttling on inbound connectors or security scanning queue backlogs.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check Exchange Admin Center Message Trace: `Get-MessageTrace -StartDate (Get-Date).AddHours(-4) -Status Pending`
2. Inspect Microsoft 365 Service Health for Incident EX820491 (Mailflow Delays).
3. Check header timestamps using Microsoft Message Header Analyzer.

### Resolution SOP
1. If message trace shows 'Deferred: 451 4.7.500 Server busy', verify tenant inbound rate limits.
2. Bypass secondary third-party email hygiene gateway temporarily if its upstream relay is throttled.
3. Whitelist high-volume automated transactional relay IP addresses in Enhanced Anti-Spam inbound connection filter.

title: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Alignment Failures Causing Outbound Quarantine
body:
### Problem Overview
Emails sent from Salesforce, ServiceNow, or marketing platforms using the `@company.com` domain are rejected with error '550 5.7.26 DMARC Policy Rejection' or delivered directly into recipient Spam folders.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Query public DNS SPF record: `dig TXT company.com +short`
2. Validate DKIM selector: `dig TXT selector1._domainkey.company.com +short`
3. Inspect DMARC XML aggregate reports (RUA) for alignment failures (DKIM vs Envelope From header mismatch).

### Resolution SOP
1. Add the SaaS provider include mechanism to SPF: e.g. `v=spf1 include:_spf.salesforce.com include:spf.protection.outlook.com ~all`.
2. Ensure total DNS lookups inside the SPF TXT record do not exceed the RFC limit of 10.
3. Configure CNAME records for custom 2048-bit DKIM key signing in the external sender platform.

title: Outlook OST Data File Corruption and Offline Sync Stalls
body:
### Problem Overview
Desktop Outlook client displays 'Disconnected' or 'Trying to connect...', crashes on launch, or freezes during search. Caused by a bloated or corrupted local offline storage table (.ost) file exceeding 45 GB.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check OST file size in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Outlook\`.
2. Run Outlook in Safe Mode: `outlook.exe /safe` to rule out conflicting COM add-ins.
3. Check Windows Application Event Log for Event ID 1000 (Faulting application name: OUTLOOK.EXE).

### Resolution SOP
1. Close Outlook and kill hanging background processes: `Stop-Process -Name OUTLOOK -Force`.
2. Rename the corrupted file to `outlook.ost.old`.
3. Reopen Outlook; Exchange will automatically generate a fresh, synchronized `.ost` file.
4. Configure Sync Slider to '1 Year' under Account Settings to prevent future bloat.

title: Microsoft 365 Shared Mailbox Permissions and Auto-Mapping Disruption
body:
### Problem Overview
Users assigned delegate access to a department shared mailbox (e.g. `billing@company.com`) cannot view the mailbox in Outlook Desktop, or receive error 'Cannot display the folder. Access denied.'

### Diagnostic Steps
1. In Exchange Online PowerShell, verify mailbox permissions: `Get-MailboxPermission -Identity "billing" -User "user@company.com"`
2. Check if AutoMapping is enabled: Look for `AutoMapping: True` in output.
3. Check Send-As and SendOnBehalf rights: `Get-RecipientPermission -Identity "billing"`

### Resolution SOP
1. Remove and re-grant permissions with AutoMapping disabled: `Remove-MailboxPermission -Identity "billing" -User "user@company.com" -AccessRights FullAccess`
2. Re-add explicitly: `Add-MailboxPermission -Identity "billing" -User "user@company.com" -AccessRights FullAccess -AutoMapping $false`
3. Manually add the shared mailbox as an additional mailbox in Outlook Account Settings -> Advanced.

title: Corporate Email Security Gateway Phishing Quarantine False Positives
body:
### Problem Overview
Legitimate client invoices and vendor contracts are blocked by the Proofpoint / Mimecast / Defender email security gateway flagged as 'High Confidence Phishing' due to URL weaponization or password-protected zip attachments.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Search Quarantine portal by Network Message ID or recipient email address.
2. Review threat intelligence verdict: Look at URL Sandbox (safe links) detonation report.
3. Inspect DMARC / SPF authentication headers for the sender.

### Resolution SOP
1. Verify sender authenticity with requester via out-of-band communication.
2. Release email from Security Admin Quarantine portal with admin override.
3. Add sender domain to Tenant Allow List with explicit domain and certificate binding.

title: GlobalProtect / AnyConnect SSL VPN Tunnel Gateway Connection Timeouts
body:
### Problem Overview
Remote employees receive 'Connection timeout (Error 504)' or 'Gateway not responding' when attempting to connect to corporate VPN gateways. Common after firewall firmware upgrades or ISP IPv6 routing issues.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Test VPN gateway TCP/443 and UDP/4501 reachability: `Test-NetConnection -ComputerName vpn.company.com -Port 443`
2. Inspect PanGPS client log: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Palo Alto Networks\GlobalProtect\PanGPS.log`
3. Check firewall portal active session limits: `show running resource-monitor`

### Resolution SOP
1. If client ISP has broken IPv6 routing, disable IPv6 on Wi-Fi adapter temporarily: `Disable-NetAdapterBinding -Name "Wi-Fi" -ComponentID ms_tcpip6`.
2. In VPN Client settings -> Preferences, clear saved portal authentication tokens.
3. Switch gateway selection from 'Auto (Geo)' to manual fallback secondary gateway (e.g. `vpn-uswest.company.com`).

title: Azure AD Conditional Access MFA Policy Evaluation Lockouts
body:
### Problem Overview
Users attempting to authenticate from remote locations or personal home offices are blocked with: 'Sign-in was blocked: You cannot access this application from your current location (Conditional Access 53003)'.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check Microsoft Entra ID -> Users -> Sign-in logs -> Conditional Access tab.
2. Identify the blocking policy: e.g. 'Block untrusted country' or 'Require Compliant Device'.
3. Review the client IP and detected GPS location against Named Locations definitions.

### Resolution SOP
1. If user is traveling internationally, create a temporary 7-day exception in the Named Locations / Trusted Countries list.
2. If device is unmanaged, guide user through Intune Company Portal device registration to achieve 'Compliant' state.
3. Reset the user's risky sign-in status in Identity Protection to clear risk flags.

title: SAML Single Sign-On (SSO) RelayState & InResponseTo Verification Errors
body:
### Problem Overview
Users clicking an enterprise SSO tile in Okta/Azure Portal receive error 'SAML response status code was Responder' or 'InResponseTo field does not match Request ID' on the target application landing page.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Capture SAML assertion payload using Chrome DevTools or SAML-tracer browser extension.
2. Verify IdP signing certificate expiration date against SP metadata.
3. Inspect system clock skew between client, IdP, and SP: Ensure drift is under 3 minutes.

### Resolution SOP
1. Synchronize server NTP clocks if clock skew exceeded allowed tolerance.
2. Update the SP Entity ID and Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL in IdP application configuration.
3. Download the renewed IdP X.509 signing certificate and upload it into the application admin security settings.

title: Okta FastPass Device Trust and Biometric Attestation Failures
body:
### Problem Overview
Engineers using Okta Verify FastPass on macOS or Windows 11 get looped into password/SMS prompts because device trust attestation fails with 'Biometrics or security key is required but not detected'.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check Okta System Log: `eventType eq "user.authentication.auth_via_mfa" and outcome.result eq "FAILURE"`
2. Check TPM 2.0 status in Windows: `Get-Tpm`
3. On macOS, check Touch ID enclave registration in Terminal: `bioutil -r`

### Resolution SOP
1. Re-enroll Windows Hello or Touch ID in OS Settings.
2. In Okta Verify app, select 'Account Details' -> 'Re-enable Touch ID / Windows Hello'.
3. If TPM state was corrupted by BIOS update, run `Clear-Tpm` and restart machine.

title: PAM CyberArk / HashiCorp Vault SSH Bastion Access Denied
body:
### Problem Overview
DevOps engineers cannot connect to production Kubernetes clusters or Linux hosts via the PAM SSH proxy bastion. Terminal output reports 'Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive)' or 'Certificate expired'.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check Vault token validity: `vault token lookup`
2. Inspect signed SSH client certificate expiry: `ssh-keygen -Lf ~/.ssh/id_rsa-cert.pub`
3. Check bastion `/var/log/secure` for SSH CA principal mismatch.

### Resolution SOP
1. Request new ephemeral certificate: `vault write -field=signed_key ssh-client-signer/sign/devops public_key=@~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub > ~/.ssh/id_rsa-cert.pub`
2. Ensure the requested principal (e.g. `ubuntu`, `ec2-user`) is listed in the user's Vault role policy.
3. Connect explicitly specifying the signed certificate: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa-cert.pub -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa bastion.corp.com`

title: Enterprise Thermal Throttling and CPU Frequency Capping on Workstations
body:
### Problem Overview
High-spec developer laptops (Dell Precision / Lenovo ThinkPad) become sluggish, with CPU frequency locked at 0.79 GHz (PROCHOT CPU throttling) even when CPU utilization is reported below 20%.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check CPU frequency in PowerShell: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object CurrentClockSpeed, MaxClockSpeed`
2. Run HWMonitor or CoreTemp to check thermal sensor temperatures (> 95°C indicates paste degradation).
3. Check Power Plan settings: `powercfg /getactivescheme`

### Resolution SOP
1. Ensure air vents are cleared of dust accumulation using compressed air.
2. Update workstation BIOS / UEFI firmware to latest release (resolves Intel DPTF firmware bugs).
3. Reset power plan: `powercfg -restoredefaultschemes` and verify 130W OEM USB-C power brick is attached instead of a 65W phone charger.

title: Dual 4K DisplayPort Flickering on Thunderbolt 4 USB-C Docks
body:
### Problem Overview
External monitors connected to Dell WD19TB / HP G4 Thunderbolt docks go black for 2–3 seconds every few minutes. Audio crackles or USB keyboard keystrokes drop simultaneously.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Open Device Manager -> System devices -> Check Thunderbolt Controller driver version.
2. Check Display Settings -> Advanced Display -> Refresh rate (ensure 60 Hz, not 59.94 Hz or unstable custom mode).
3. Verify DisplayPort 1.4 HBR3 vs DSC (Display Stream Compression) support in dock management utility.

### Resolution SOP
1. Flash Thunderbolt Dock firmware using manufacturer utility (e.g. Dell Dock Firmware Update Tool).
2. Replace passive DisplayPort cables with VESA-certified DP 1.4 or active HDMI 2.1 cables.
3. In Intel Graphics Command Center, turn OFF 'Panel Self-Refresh' and 'Display Power Saving Technology'.

title: Zebra Thermal Industrial Barcode Printer Driver Spooler Crashes
body:
### Problem Overview
Warehouse and shipping stations cannot print 4x6 packing labels. Print jobs stall in queue with status 'Error - Printing', and the Windows Print Spooler service (`spoolsv.exe`) crashes repeatedly.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check Print Spooler service status: `Get-Service spooler`
2. Check Event Viewer -> Applications and Services -> Microsoft -> Windows -> PrintService -> Operational for Event ID 372.
3. Inspect corrupt spool files in `%SystemRoot%\System32\spool\PRINTERS\`.

### Resolution SOP
1. Stop Print Spooler: `Stop-Service spooler -Force`
2. Purge stuck spool buffer files: `Remove-Item C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\* -Force`
3. Restart spooler: `Start-Service spooler`
4. Upgrade printer driver to ZDesigner v10.x and calibrate label gap sensor via Zebra Setup Utilities.

title: NVMe SSD Controller S.M.A.R.T. Read-Only Fail-Safe Recovery
body:
### Problem Overview
Laptops lock up with Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) `CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED`. On reboot, BIOS reports 'No bootable device found' or the disk is mounted read-only due to NVMe SSD endurance exhaustion.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. In Windows PowerShell: `Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter | Select-Object Wear, ReadErrorsTotal`
2. In Linux Live USB: `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1`
3. Check Percentage Used attribute (> 100% means spare blocks exhausted).

### Resolution SOP
1. If read-only, boot into Live Linux USB and image user data immediately: `ddrescue /dev/nvme0n1 /mnt/backup/drive.img`
2. Dispatch replacement PCIe Gen4 NVMe drive under manufacturer enterprise warranty.
3. Image new SSD with standard corporate Windows 11 Enterprise SOE.

title: Conference Room Microphones and USB Polycom Audio Dropouts
body:
### Problem Overview
Meeting room Microsoft Teams Rooms (MTR) systems fail to detect the Poly Studio USB video bar. Participants report robotic audio or 'Microphone not found' during scheduled video calls.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check Teams Room Settings -> Peripherals -> Audio Input.
2. In Windows Device Manager, inspect Universal Serial Bus controllers for Code 43 (Device Descriptor Request Failed).
3. Check powered USB extender link LED (Crestron / Extron USB-over-CAT6).

### Resolution SOP
1. Power-cycle the Poly Studio unit and the USB-over-CAT6 transceiver boxes.
2. In Device Manager, right-click the malfunctioning USB Root Hub -> Disable then Re-enable.
3. Disable USB Selective Suspend in Power Options: `powercfg /SETACVALUEINDEX SCHEME_CURRENT 2a737441-1930-4402-8d77-b2bebba4d5a0 48e6b7a6-50f5-4782-a5d4-53bb8f07e226 0`

title: Silent MSI / Intune Application Packaging Deployment Error 1603
body:
### Problem Overview
Enterprise software (e.g. Cisco Webex, Docker Desktop, Autodesk) pushed via Microsoft Intune fails on client devices with generic failure code `0x80070643` or Windows Installer Error `1603` (Fatal error during installation).

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Inspect Intune Management Extension log: `C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs\AgentExecutor.log`
2. Open verbose MSI installation log: Search for `Return value 3` (indicates the exact failing action).
3. Verify pending system reboot status: `Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing\RebootPending'`

### Resolution SOP
1. If a reboot is pending from monthly Windows updates, restart the machine before retrying install.
2. Uninstall previous partial version using Microsoft Program Install and Uninstall troubleshooter utility.
3. Add required silent flags and suppress restart: `msiexec /i package.msi /qn /norestart /l*v C:\temp\install.log`

title: macOS Application Gatekeeper Unsigned Developer Notarization Blocks
body:
### Problem Overview
macOS Sequoia / Sonoma users attempting to open internal developer utilities receive a modal prompt: 'App cannot be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software' or 'App is damaged and can\'t be opened'.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Inspect extended file attributes: `xattr -l /Applications/InternalTool.app`
2. Look for `com.apple.quarantine` attribute tag.
3. Verify code signature: `codesign -dv --verbose=4 /Applications/InternalTool.app`

### Resolution SOP
1. For verified internal apps, remove quarantine flag: `sudo xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/InternalTool.app`
2. In System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Click 'Open Anyway' under Security.
3. Ensure enterprise build pipeline signs binaries with Apple Developer Enterprise ID and submits for notarization: `xcrun notarytool submit`

title: Visual Studio Code / JetBrains Remote SSH Host Key Fingerprint Mismatches
body:
### Problem Overview
Developers using VS Code Remote - SSH or JetBrains Gateway cannot connect to remote development EC2/VM instances. Error: 'Host key verification failed. The authenticity of host cannot be established. Remote host identification has changed!'.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Read error message for offending line number in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`.
2. Confirm instance re-provisioning or IP address reassignment with cloud engineering.

### Resolution SOP
1. Remove stale fingerprint from known hosts: `ssh-keygen -R <server-ip-or-hostname>`
2. Connect once manually in terminal to accept and cache new ECDSA/ED25519 fingerprint: `ssh user@<server-ip>`
3. Reopen VS Code Remote SSH session.

title: Node.js & Python Enterprise Proxy SSL Self-Signed CA Certificate Failures
body:
### Problem Overview
Developers running `npm install`, `pip install`, or `git clone` on corporate networks receive SSL handshake failures: `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN` or `certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain`.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Identify corporate TLS inspection proxy (Zscaler, Netskope, Palo Alto Prisma).
2. Check if Python / Node.js is using its bundled CA store instead of Windows / macOS system Keychain.

### Resolution SOP
1. For Node.js / NPM: Configure corporate CA certificate path: `npm config set cafile "C:\Certs\CorporateRootCA.crt"`
2. For Python: Install `pip-system-certs` or set environment variable: `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE="/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"`
3. For Git: `git config --global http.sslCAInfo "C:/Certs/CorporateRootCA.crt"`

title: Windows Sandbox & WSL2 Virtualized Nested Hyper-V Conflicts
body:
### Problem Overview
Developers installing WSL2 or Docker Desktop receive: 'WslRegisterDistribution failed with error: 0x80370102' or 'Hardware-assisted virtualization is disabled in the BIOS'.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check virtualization status in Task Manager -> Performance -> CPU -> 'Virtualization: Enabled'.
2. In PowerShell: `Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName VirtualMachinePlatform`
3. Check hypervisor launch type: `bcdedit /enum | findstr hypervisorlaunchtype`

### Resolution SOP
1. Enable hypervisor in BCD: `bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype auto`
2. Enable required Windows features: `dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:VirtualMachinePlatform /all /norestart`
3. Restart physical machine and verify Intel VT-x / AMD-V is enabled in motherboard BIOS settings.

title: Active Directory BadPwdCount Account Lockout Loop Detection
body:
### Problem Overview
An employee's Active Directory domain account locks out repeatedly within seconds of being unlocked by IT support. Workstation displays 'Your account has been locked. Contact your support person.'

### Diagnostic Steps
1. In PowerShell ActiveDirectory module, locate locking source computer: `Get-ADUser -Identity <username> -Properties BadPwdCount, badPasswordTime, LockedOut`
2. Inspect Security Event Log on Primary Domain Controller for Event ID 4740 (A user account was locked out) -> Check 'Caller Computer Name'.

### Resolution SOP
1. Identify the caller device (often a mobile phone with an expired ActiveSync password, stale Wi-Fi profile, or scheduled batch script).
2. On caller computer, open Windows Credential Manager -> Clear stored generic credentials under Windows Credentials.
3. Check for lingering mapped network drives: `net use * /delete /yes`
4. Unlock account in AD: `Unlock-ADAccount -Identity <username>`

title: Kerberos Pre-Authentication Clock Skew Authentication Timeouts
body:
### Problem Overview
Users cannot log into domain workstations or access corporate file shares, receiving error: 'The system cannot log you on due to clock skew' or Kerberos error `KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW` (Event ID 14).

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Compare local workstation system time against Domain Controller time: `net time \\dc01.corp.local`
2. Kerberos protocol permits a maximum drift of 5 minutes (300 seconds).
3. Check Windows Time service status: `w32tm /query /status`

### Resolution SOP
1. Unregister and re-register Windows Time service on client: `w32tm /unregister && w32tm /register`
2. Force immediate resynchronization with PDC emulator: `w32tm /resync /force`
3. Purge existing tickets: `klist purge` and re-authenticate.

title: AWS IAM AssumeRole Token Expiration and Session Permission Boundaries
body:
### Problem Overview
Developers running Terraform or AWS CLI receive `AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole` or `ExpiredToken: The security token included in the request is expired` during production deployment workflows.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check current identity: `aws sts get-caller-identity`
2. Check role Trust Relationship policy: Verify `Principal` includes the IAM user or SAML federated role.
3. Check IAM Permissions Boundary attached to the role.

### Resolution SOP
1. If session expired, re-authenticate via AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO): `aws sso login --profile production`
2. Increase max session duration on the IAM role from 1 hour to 4 hours in AWS Console.
3. Ensure MFA token is supplied if the role requires `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: true`.

title: Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) Telephony Loop Failure
body:
### Problem Overview
Remote employees locked out of their accounts cannot complete Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR). SMS codes never arrive on their mobile phones, or Microsoft phone call verification drops immediately.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check user authentication methods in Entra Admin Center -> Users -> Authentication methods.
2. Verify mobile phone number country code formatting (must be E.164 format: e.g. `+1 5550192834`).
3. Check carrier SMS delivery status in Azure Monitor Audit logs.

### Resolution SOP
1. IT Service Desk performs verified identity check via secure video call.
2. Generate a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) in Entra ID admin center (valid for 8 hours).
3. Direct user to `myaccount.microsoft.com` using the TAP to re-register Microsoft Authenticator push notifications.

title: GitHub Enterprise Organization SAML Member De-provisioning Sync Lag
body:
### Problem Overview
Contractors or transferred employees retain access to internal GitHub repositories hours after departure, or newly onboarded engineers cannot see internal repositories after Okta assignment.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. In GitHub Enterprise Cloud -> Organization -> Settings -> Audit Log: Filter by `action:org.add_member`.
2. In Okta -> Applications -> GitHub Enterprise -> Push Groups tab: Look for SCIM synchronization errors.

### Resolution SOP
1. In Okta, click 'Push Now' on the desynchronized engineering security group.
2. If SCIM bearer token is expired, generate a new Personal Access Token (PAT) with `admin:org` scope and rebind in Okta.
3. Manually revoke SAML identity link in GitHub Org Settings -> SAML SSO -> Manage members.

title: PostgreSQL RDS Connection Pool Exhaustion and Deadlock Resolution
body:
### Problem Overview
Backend microservices report `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections` or `500 Internal Server Error`. Database active connections reach 100% of `max_connections`.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Connect via superuser psql and inspect active queries: `SELECT pid, usename, state, now() - query_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle' ORDER BY duration DESC;`
2. Check for lock blocking tree: `SELECT blocked_locks.pid AS blocked_pid, blocking_locks.pid AS blocking_pid FROM pg_catalog.pg_locks blocked_locks...`
3. Inspect RDS CloudWatch metric `DatabaseConnections`.

### Resolution SOP
1. Terminate long-running locking queries gracefully: `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(<pid>);` (or `pg_terminate_backend(<pid>)` if unyielding).
2. Deploy PgBouncer or AWS RDS Proxy between applications and Postgres to multiplex client connections.
3. Ensure applications configure idle client timeout (`idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '30s'`).

title: MySQL InnoDB Log Sequence Gap and Replication Thread Lag
body:
### Problem Overview
Read-replica MySQL instances fall behind master by thousands of seconds (`Seconds_Behind_Master > 3600`). Reporting dashboards query stale data and replica disk fills rapidly with relay logs.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. On replica: `SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G` (or `SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G`).
2. Check `Last_Error_Number` (e.g. 1062 Duplicate entry or 1032 Key not found).
3. Inspect multi-threaded replica worker status: `SHOW PROCESSLIST`.

### Resolution SOP
1. Enable multi-threaded applier: `SET GLOBAL replica_parallel_workers = 8; SET GLOBAL replica_parallel_type = 'LOGICAL_CLOCK';`
2. If replication broke due to a non-critical schema mismatch, inject GTID skip transaction: `SET GTID_NEXT='<gtid_set>'; BEGIN; COMMIT; SET GTID_NEXT='AUTOMATIC'; START REPLICA;`
3. Rebuild replica from automated Percona XtraBackup snapshot if sequence divergence is permanent.

title: Redis Cluster Out-of-Memory Eviction Key Retention Spikes
body:
### Problem Overview
Application sessions drop randomly and cache write commands fail with: `OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'`. Redis cluster CPU reaches 100% due to key eviction thrashing.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Connect with redis-cli: `redis-cli -h <cluster-node> info memory`
2. Scan for top memory consuming keys: `redis-cli --bigkeys`
3. Check current eviction policy: `CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy`

### Resolution SOP
1. Change eviction policy to volatile-lru or allkeys-lru: `CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`
2. Ensure all application session cache keys include an explicit TTL expiration (e.g. `EXPIRE session:abc 86400`).
3. Scale Redis ElastiCache node type or add cluster shards to distribute memory load.

title: MongoDB Replica Set Election Split-Brain Quorum Loss
body:
### Problem Overview
MongoDB cluster drops writes with error `NotWritablePrimary` or `Server selection timeout after 30000 ms`. All replica set members are in `SECONDARY` or `RECOVERING` state.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. In mongosh: `rs.status()`
2. Check member voting status: `rs.conf().members`
3. Inspect mongod logs for network partition heartbeats: `Heartbeat to <host> failed: NetworkTimeout`.

### Resolution SOP
1. Verify network connectivity between all nodes on port 27017.
2. If an arbiter node crashed causing quorum loss in a 3-node set, temporarily force reconfig: `cfg = rs.conf(); cfg.members[2].votes = 0; rs.reconfig(cfg, {force: true})`
3. Restart secondary node with corrupted oplog in repair mode.

title: SQL Server TempDB Filegroup Autogrowth Storage Saturation
body:
### Problem Overview
Production Microsoft SQL Server databases freeze with error 1105: 'Could not allocate space for object in database tempdb because the PRIMARY filegroup is full'. Transactions rollback immediately.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check TempDB drive free space using Windows Explorer or `EXEC xp_fixeddrives`.
2. Identify queries consuming TempDB internal objects: `SELECT session_id, internal_objects_alloc_page_count, user_objects_alloc_page_count FROM sys.dm_db_session_space_usage ORDER BY internal_objects_alloc_page_count DESC`
3. Check for massive un-indexed sorting or hash joins in execution plans.

### Resolution SOP
1. Kill the runaway report query session: `KILL <session_id>`
2. Shrink TempDB data files: `DBCC SHRINKDATABASE(tempdb, 10)`
3. Pre-size TempDB files across multiple dedicated disk spindles with equal autogrowth settings (64 MB increments).

title: Kubernetes Pod CrashLoopBackOff Triggered by OOMKilled Memory Limits
body:
### Problem Overview
Application microservice pods continuously restart in production Kubernetes clusters. `kubectl get pods` shows status `CrashLoopBackOff` with `RESTARTS` count incrementing every 2 minutes.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Inspect pod exit code: `kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n production`
2. Look for `Last State: Terminated`, `Reason: OOMKilled`, `Exit Code: 137`.
3. Check current memory utilization curve in Grafana or Datadog.

### Resolution SOP
1. If application requires more working memory, increase deployment resource limits in Helm chart: `resources.limits.memory: 2Gi` (up from 512Mi).
2. For Java/Node apps, set heap allocation flags explicitly: e.g. `--max-old-space-size=1536` for Node or `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75` for Java.
3. Inspect code for memory leaks (unclosed streams, unbounded in-memory caches, retaining unreferenced objects).

title: JVM Heap Garbage Collection Pauses and Tenured Generation Leaks
body:
### Problem Overview
Java Spring Boot microservices experience sudden latency spikes from 30ms to 8,000ms. Health check endpoints time out, causing AWS ALB to cycle containers out of target groups.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check GC logs: Look for `Full GC (Allocation Failure)` pauses exceeding 3,000ms.
2. Capture thread dump: `jcmd <pid> Thread.print`
3. Capture heap dump on OOM: Verify `-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError` generated `.hprof` file.

### Resolution SOP
1. Switch GC algorithm to low-latency ZGC or G1GC: `-XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200`
2. Analyze `.hprof` file with Eclipse Memory Analyzer (MAT) to identify leak suspects (e.g. static HashMaps).
3. Ensure container has adequate CPU resources: GC threads starve when CPU throttling is triggered.

title: Node.js Microservice Event-Loop Latency Spikes Under Concurrent Load
body:
### Problem Overview
Node.js API servers show low CPU and memory utilization (30%), yet response times degrade exponentially under load. Prometheus reports `nodejs_eventloop_lag_seconds` exceeding 1.5 seconds.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Profile CPU activity using Node Inspector: `node --cpu-prof index.js`
2. Check for synchronous blocking operations: Synchronous regex (`eval-regex`), `JSON.parse` on 50MB files, or `fs.readFileSync`.
3. Check crypto hashing operations on the main event thread.

### Resolution SOP
1. Offload heavy computational work (cryptography, PDF generation) to Worker Threads or BullMQ background worker queue.
2. Replace synchronous fs calls with `fs.promises`.
3. Scale horizontally using Node.js Cluster mode or increase Kubernetes replica count.

title: AWS Elastic Load Balancer (ALB) 504 Gateway Timeouts During Peak Traffic
body:
### Problem Overview
End users encounter `504 Gateway Time-out` during marketing campaigns or batch data syncs. AWS ALB CloudWatch metrics show elevated `HTTPCode_ELB_504_Count` and spikes in `TargetResponseTime`.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Check ALB access logs in S3: Filter by `target_status_code == "-"` (indicates backend failed to respond within idle timeout).
2. Check backend EC2 / ECS container CPU and connection queues.
3. Compare ALB idle timeout (default 60s) with backend web server keepalive timeout.

### Resolution SOP
1. Ensure backend keep-alive timeout is GREATER than ALB idle timeout (e.g. Nginx `keepalive_timeout 65;`).
2. Scale Target Group capacity via Auto Scaling Policy triggered on `RequestCountPerTarget`.
3. Optimize slow SQL queries and external third-party API calls holding backend threads open.

title: Nginx Ingress Controller Upstream Buffer Overflow and 502 Bad Gateway
body:
### Problem Overview
Requests with large JWT headers or bulk JSON payloads fail with `502 Bad Gateway`. Ingress controller logs report: `upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream`.

### Diagnostic Steps
1. Inspect Nginx ingress controller pod logs: `kubectl logs -n ingress-nginx -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx | grep 502`
2. Inspect request header size (cookie payload size + OAuth token).

### Resolution SOP
1. Add buffer annotations to the Ingress resource:
   `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size: "128k"`
   `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffers-number: "4"`
   `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-busy-buffers-size: "256k"`
2. In backend application, trim excessive Set-Cookie headers on redirects.
3. Reload ingress configuration and verify successful 200 OK responses.
